traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and technical requirements for story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS are implemented and verified.
The rule is correctly exposed under the canonical name `prefer-supports-annotation` with `prefer-implements-annotation` as a deprecated alias. It is disabled by default and can be configured via standard ESLint severities (off/warn/error). When enabled, it: - Detects legacy `@story` + `@req` blocks and emits a recommendation (`preferImplements`) with safe auto-fix for simple, single-story cases (single @story path, one or more simple @req lines). - Converts these to a single `@supports` line while preserving JSDoc structure and comment formatting. - Detects and reports but does not auto-fix multi-story or mixed-@supports usages via `cannotAutoFix` and `multiStoryDetected` messages.
Legacy `@story`/`@req` annotations remain valid when the rule is disabled, and even with the rule enabled, non-target patterns (only @story, only @req, only @supports, or specific mixed-but-incomplete forms) are intentionally ignored, preserving backward compatibility.
Comprehensive unit tests and documentation (rule docs plus migration guide) align with the story’s examples and configuration guidance, and the full Jest suite passes, confirming the behavior. Therefore this story is fully implemented and passes.
